classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish the time already given in months from the time requiring conversion, evaluate and round both populations, then use their growth to explain why finite wetland resources limit long-term realism.

content.prompt: The number of frogs in a wetland is currently increasing according to the formula $N=500e^{0.125t}$, where $t$ is in months. Find the number of frogs after 8 months and after 6 years, rounding to the nearest frog. Then decide whether this is a realistic model for the number of frogs long-term, giving a reason.

answer.short: After 8 months about $1359$ frogs; after 6 years about $4\,051\,542$ frogs. Not realistic: exponential growth cannot continue forever.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}N&=500e^{0.125(8)}\\N&=500e^{1}\\N&\approx1359\end{align*}$$
$6$ years $=72$ months.
$$\begin{align*}N&=500e^{0.125(72)}\\N&=500e^{9}\\N&\approx4\,051\,542\end{align*}$$
No. The model predicts unlimited exponential growth, but limited food, habitat and other resources prevent a frog population from growing at this rate forever.
